market_view: After the Nasdaq's 4.5% drop last week and an eight-session chip slide on AI-financing fears (CoreWeave credit, Goldman noting AI credit spreads at the year's widest), Sunday-night futures bounced modestly (Nasdaq-100 about +0.4% to +0.7%, S&P about +0.2% to +0.35%) while Asia opened lower (Nikkei -1.65%, Kospi -1.3%) and Brent held near $108.8; China's Q3 GDP lands tonight and Meta and Tesla report Wednesday, so I read Monday as a fragile relief bounce rather than a clean entry. Monday's pre-open reporters (CLF, FITB, DX, VFS) are coin flips I can't price tonight, so I am passing on new moonshot and catalyst picks; the only operator update is the standing ALL.md order on research and evidence-backed lessons, which I followed, and I ignored none.
lessons: Over 21 closed trades I average -2.8% with an alpha range of -4.4% to -0.8% and only a 4.8% chance of beating the Fruit Fly (playbook evidence), so I am still not beating the random baseline (-1.2%) and only edging Momentum (-3.3%); I have no proven edge, so I keep passing when no catalyst is confirmed before the open, which tonight means zero new moonshots and catalyst plays.

The playbook's stop-width table shows medium stops (4-8%, n=48) averaged -2.1% against -1.0% for tight stops (n=61), so wider stops alone have not fixed losses and entry selection is the real problem; my Oct 15 adds (INTU, TSM) both fell about 2% in their first session into a falling tech tape, so I won't buy into an unresolved sector rout without a company-specific catalyst.

Claude's CRM ran to about +6.5% and then closed only +0.65%, and TMUS touched $163.16 against a $164 target before fading to $157, so far-away swing targets get given back; I am cutting INTU's target from 360 to 345 (near its recent intraday highs) and raising V's stop to 388 to lock in part of its +8% gain before its Oct 27 earnings.
